newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* Foundation Health Corp and Health Systems International Inc announced that they would merge to form a $6.4 billion company with nearly five million affiliates.
* Anthem Inc confirmed that it planned to add Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Connecticut to its Anthem East unit.

* U.S. President Bill Clinton's administration offered to remove all export limits on data scrambling technology if computer companies agreed to allow law enforcement officers to unscramble communications without the use of a key to the code.
* The European Union said it would challenge in a new World Trade Organization court a U.S. law that imposes sanctions against foreign companies that do business in Cuba.
* Chrysler Corp's car and truck sales rose 22 percent in September, while sales at General Motors Corp fell 2.1 percent compared to the same period last year.
* General Motors Corp is discussing compromises with the United Automobile Workers and Canadian Automobile Workers in an effort to reach new national labor contracts.
* Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc proposed to the New York State Public Service Commission to freeze its electric rates for five years.
* The U.S. Senate passed the National Securities Markets Improvement Act that streamlines regulation of mutual funds, investment advisers and stock brokers.
* HCIA Inc said its earnings for the quarter would be $0.10 per share to $0.15 per share instead of the projected $0.29.
